principle: The owner-command path accepts only enumerated actions from an authenticated actor. Every command is schema-validated against an allowlist, checks its expected_current_hash (compare-and-swap) against live state, records a dry-run summary, and would append a decision event and CAS-update only the affected state. No arbitrary shell or free-form field is ever accepted. A stale or unauthorized command fails safely and mutates nothing.

actions.affects: revision request on an exact object
integration to dev of an exact reviewed head
one non-force compare-and-swap migration of the exact released scheduler state into the exact reviewed v2 implementation while dispatch remains frozen

one create-missing-only mutation of the exact authenticated GitHub Project field schema with a separate append-only INTENT/RESULT audit-ref CAS chain; item content, tickets, backfill and dev delivery remain forbidden

one atomic exact-lease publication of the owner authority commit A, the exact prebuilt reconciled scheduler state S1, and any create-if-absent late-candidate quarantine refs; unavailable candidate objects retain custody and WITHHOLD publication
one atomic two-ref compare-and-swap publication of exact prebuilt scheduler state S1 and development D1 from exact all-off predecessors S0 and D0
release / main / publication of an exact object (owner-exclusive)
OWNER_OVERRIDE recorded separately from the evidence it overrides (owner-exclusive)

rules.enumerated_only: A command whose action is not in this allowlist is rejected.
rules.authenticated_actor: The command actor must map to a role in the action's authenticator_roles.
rules.owner_exclusive: authorize-scheduler-migration, authorize-project-schema-change, authorize-scheduler-state-reconciliation, authorize-scheduler-cutover, authorize-release and record-owner-override authenticate the owner role only.
rules.compare_and_swap: When requires_cas is true, expected_current_hash must equal the live sealed hash of the target; a mismatch is a stale command and fails safely.
rules.no_arbitrary_input: The request schema forbids additional fields; there is no shell or free-form command field.
rules.dry_run_first: The processor records a dry-run summary before any mutation; --apply performs the mutation only after the same validation passes.
rules.declared_lifecycle_target: An action may declare lifecycle_target. Applying it moves the target capsule to that state only if transitions.json declares that exact transition from the capsule's current state and permits the authenticating role (the owner role is permitted on protected transitions). An undeclared or unpermitted transition is rejected and nothing is written.
rules.blocker_resolution: An action may declare resolves_blocker. Applying it clears the target capsule's blocker, because the decision the blocker was waiting on has been recorded. A deferral or a routing-only action never clears one.
rules.append_only_apply: Applying writes one append-only decision event and re-seals only the target capsule under compare-and-swap. It never rewrites history, never edits an existing event, and never touches another ticket.
rules.scheduler_migration_binding: authorize-scheduler-migration is valid for one use before its expiry only. Its structured scheduler_migration object binds the exact reviewed code head and tree; exact released source state OID, tree, snapshot hash, journal manifest and event count; canonical anchor; preserved unrelated local tip; frozen dispatch; state versions; target ref; expected remote OID; ordinary non-force forward-only compare-and-swap; and abort-on-remote-change.
rules.project_schema_change_binding: authorize-project-schema-change is valid for one attempt before its expiry only. Its structured project_schema_change object binds the exact reviewed executor head and tree; Project identity, authenticated login and write scope; observed Project update instant; complete field, item and value preflight counts and roots; pagination, Priority and ordered definition manifests; create-missing-only mode; forbidden item, ticket and backfill mutations; and abort-on-Project-change. Read-only preflight proves refs/heads/agentops/project-schema-audit is absent. This exact packet alone authorizes one deterministic initial audit commit derived as a child of the owner authority commit and one create-if-absent publication; that commit contains only attempt and INTENT facts and never predicts a future receipt or manifest object. Subsequent attempt, journal and sealed receipt commits form an ordinary non-force forward-only linear CAS chain on that audit ref under the leased .agentops/scheduler/project-schema-attempts subtree using canonical paths and an INTENT-before-each-create and RESULT-after-each-response protocol. The sealed receipt embeds a non-circular project-field-readback; only afterward may one final direct-child audit commit add the separate exact nine-field cutover manifest, including its Project updated instant, whose parsed source_receipt_hash names that sealed receipt. The closed local audit result is constructed only after manifest publication and the single postinspection. It records only the final published object, raw create and manifest-CAS exit codes, manifest blob/SHA, and the observed audit ref/OID; it contains no asserted parent, expected-OID, filename, source-link, equality, outcome, or success fields. The semantic verifier derives exact ancestry, allowed paths, manifest filename and source receipt, and publication success from the committed objects and observed ref. Every consumed GraphQL create is never retried; recovery inspects once without issuing creates; ref recreation and dev mutation remain forbidden without separate exact authority.
rules.scheduler_state_reconciliation_binding: authorize-scheduler-state-reconciliation v2 is valid for one attempt before its expiry only. Its closed structured payload binds the exact reviewed reconciler head and tree; a canonical PASS-only independent QA artifact whose every test exited zero; exact source S0 and prebuilt target S1 state OIDs, trees, snapshot hashes, journal manifests and event counts; exact closed machine custody; the complete canonically ordered work-lease disposition; no-refill quiet-window delta; exact D0 and S0 remote predecessors; and the complete canonically ordered late-candidate preservation plan. Every available late candidate binds its candidate commit and tree either to an already-existing immutable remote ref at that exact OID or to a canonical create-if-absent quarantine ref included in the same atomic push. A missing, corrupt, unreachable or non-byte-recoverable candidate object requires a closed owner retain-custody-and-withhold disposition that binds nullable expected tree/blob/hash facts, every recorded base OID, and a canonical recovery-evidence artifact; conflicting base evidence is recorded explicitly and never resolved by guesswork. Any unavailable disposition forbids custody clear, state publication and silent omission. The authority event A is constructed locally as the direct child of D0 and never predicts its own OID. S1 is prebuilt as the direct child of S0. The sole mutating publication is one git push --atomic carrying A, S1 and every new quarantine ref with exact leases. Existing immutable pins are read-only preconditions. Mixed, missing or ambiguous postconditions are inspected once and WITHHOLD without retry. A closed non-circular local result receipt records only constructed A and observed S1 objects, raw atomic transport facts, and the state, development and candidate refs/OIDs seen in one postinspection; it contains no asserted parents, expected-OID copies, exactness, outcome, custody-clear or success claims. The semantic verifier derives candidate/head equality, QA binding and independence, source/target ancestry, exact field ordering, complete lease and late-candidate coverage, ref/OID equality, and permission to clear custody.
rules.scheduler_cutover_binding: authorize-scheduler-cutover is valid for one attempt before its expiry only. Its structured scheduler_cutover object binds the exact reviewed scheduler head and tree; canonical schema, path, Git blob OID, SHA-256 and closed parsed semantics for a PASS-only independent QA receipt whose every test passed with exit code zero, the COMPLETE Project-schema result, the exact ordered nine-field Project manifest including Project updated instant and exact text/select option structures, quiet-window receipt, migration event, released machine custody, legacy activation, pre-cutover scheduler config, exact post-cutover scheduler config and activation manifest. The activation-manifest blob must parse and deep-equal the inline structural template. The semantic verifier, not inert assertion text, checks template D0/S0 against the expected remote OIDs and current-state tree, every repeated blob, QA candidate and independence, receipt/manifest linkage, quiet-window source, and migration-event location. The all-off matrix requires scheduler dispatch false, legacy-watcher authority false, scheduler authorization evidence null, migration dispatch frozen true, legacy activation false, and legacy mode STOOD_DOWN_FOR_SCHEDULER_CUTOVER. The fillable authority input names only existing D0/S0 objects and source evidence; it never predicts A, S1 or D1 identities whose bytes depend on the authority event. The template structurally enumerates A's exact source, evidence and deterministic render paths; S1's single typed activation event, snapshot update and byte-preserved state paths; and D1's sole scheduler-config change to the exact post-cutover blob. A closed local result receipt records only constructed A/S1/D1 OIDs and trees, activation/config blobs, raw atomic transport facts, and the two refs and OIDs observed during one postinspection. It contains no asserted parents, expected-OID copies, exactness, outcome, or dispatch claims. The semantic verifier derives ancestry, equality, and permission to dispatch solely from committed objects and observed refs. The sole publication is one git push --atomic of S1 and D1 with exact compare-and-swap leases against S0 and D0. expected_development_remote_oid always names D0, never A or D1.
rules.protected_action_non_substitution: The four scheduler protected actions are distinct and non-substitutable. Free-form reason, params, chat, blanket authority, record-owner-override, migration authority, Project-schema authority, reconciliation authority, cutover authority, exact-head QA, a prior use, an opaque hash without its canonical path and Git blob binding, or an artifact that fails its own schema and semantic checks cannot supply or broaden another action's structured payload.
rules.protected_action_consumption: For the four scheduler protected actions, execution begins only after the complete structured payload validates. The packet is consumed on its first apply attempt. A partial, failed, timed-out or ambiguous external result is inspected exactly once and never retried. Reconciliation may clear custody only when A, S1 and every late-candidate pin equal their exact postconditions and no unavailable disposition exists. Cutover may dispatch only when both protected refs equal exact S1 and D1. Any mixed, missing or neither result is WITHHOLD and requires fresh evidence and owner authority.
